title: Starting a compost bin at home
body: Keep a small covered bin for fruit and vegetable scraps, egg shells, and coffee grounds. Turn it every week or two and keep it slightly damp — in a few weeks it breaks down into usable soil.

title: What husk can actually become
body: Coconut husk isn't just discarded fiber — it's spun into coir rope and matting, used as a growing medium for plants, and pressed into biodegradable packaging.

title: Setting waste aside for pickup
body: A dedicated bin kept separate from general trash, emptied at the same time each day, is enough to make a shop or stall's waste usable rather than contaminated.

title: Why 'ugly' produce still has value
body: Bruised or misshapen fruit is often nutritionally identical to what's sold on shelves. It's a strong candidate for animal feed or juicing before it spoils further.

title: How biogas digesters work, roughly
body: Organic waste is sealed in an oxygen-free tank where bacteria break it down, releasing methane that's captured and burned for cooking gas or electricity instead of escaping into the air.

title: What makes a listing easy to collect
body: A rough weight, a clear pickup window, and a specific location get a listing claimed faster than a vague 'some waste available' post.
